title: A generic geometric orbit gives a finite universal-homeomorphism quotient on a dense open
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $B$ be a nonempty finite disjoint union of integral finite-type $e$-schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $Y$ be a reduced quasi-projective finite-type $e$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-kun-projective]. Here quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into finite-dimensional projective space over $e$. Let a finite group $G$ act by $e$-scheme automorphisms on $Y$. Suppose $h:Y\to B$ is invariant, projective and surjective [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], sends every generic point to a generic point of $B$ with finite residue-field extension [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field], and the underlying points of each geometric generic fibre of $h$ form a single $G$-orbit [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. For every subgroup $H\leq G$ there exist a finite surjective admissible scheme quotient $q_H:Y\to Q_H$ [def-per-admissible-finite-scheme-quotient] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $d_H:Q_H\to B$ with $d_H q_H=h$. Each $q_H$ has orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaf and is categorical for invariant morphisms to arbitrary schemes; $Q_H$ is reduced. There is a dense open $U\subseteq B$ containing every generic point such that $h^{-1}U\to U$ and $Q_G\times_B U\to U$ are finite, and the latter is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. The generic fibre of $d_G$ over each integral component of $B$ is the spectrum of a finite purely inseparable extension of its function field [def-pc-field-tower]. No normality of $Y$ or $B$, no faithful or free group action, and no restriction on the group order are imposed.

proof.text: First $Y$ is separated over $e$. Indeed its locally closed immersion $j:Y\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^n_e$ is a monomorphism. Thus $\Delta_{Y/e}$ is the pullback of $\Delta_{P/e}$ along $j\times j:Y\times_eY\to P\times_eP$: the pullback is $Y\times_PY=Y$. Projective space is separated and closed immersions remain closed after base change. This checks the separatedness hypothesis of the quotient theorem without imposing any separatedness condition on $B$.

source.place: Tag 01NH, lemma-projective-space-separated; morphisms.tex Tag 01QR, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion; elementary diagonal pullback

proof.text: For every $H\leq G$, apply the finite-type field quotient theorem to $Y/e$ and the restricted action. Its final clause supplies admissibility for every such action because $Y$ is quasi-projective. It gives a finite surjective $q_H:Y\to Q_H$, the orbit geometric fibres, topological quotient, invariant structure sheaf, categorical property for all scheme targets, and reducedness of $Q_H$. Invariance of $h$ gives a unique factor $d_H:Q_H\to B$ with $d_Hq_H=h$. These properties are exactly the admissible quotient definition. The identity $h=d_Hq_H$ and surjectivity of $h$ imply surjectivity of $d_H$.

source.place: IX 1.4, printed pp.132--133; X 2.3 Step 2, p.151; quotient theorem applied separately to each subgroup

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, and finite type over a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian; hence $B$ and $Y$ are Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, so both are quasi-separated. Since $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ factors as $Y\to B\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ and is of finite type, $h$ is locally of finite type. As $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $B$ is quasi-separated, $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of a component $B_i$ and $\bar\eta$ the geometric point over it. The projection $Y_{\bar\eta}\to Y_\eta$ is surjective, being the base change of the surjection $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(\eta)}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$, and $Y_\eta$ is homeomorphic to $h^{-1}(\eta)$. The underlying points of $Y_{\bar\eta}$ form one orbit of the finite group $G$, so they are finitely many; hence $h^{-1}(\eta)$ is finite. The generic-finiteness lemma now gives a dense open $V\subseteq B$ containing every generic point with $h^{-1}V\to V$ finite. By the last relative clause of the quotient theorem, $Q_G\times_BV\to V$ is also finite. For each of the finitely many components $B_i$, choose a nonempty affine $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i\subseteq V\cap B_i$; then $A_i$ is a Noetherian domain. These opens are disjoint and contain all generic points.

source.place: Tag 02NW (lemma-generically-finite); Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian) and 01T8 (lemma-permanence-finite-type); properties.tex Tag 01OY (lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated); ILO X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151

proof.text: Fix $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A$, put $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$, and write $Q_G\times_BU_i=\operatorname{Spec}C$. Finiteness and base change give the generic fibre $\operatorname{Spec}D$, where $D=C\otimes_AK=(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}C$ is finite-dimensional over $K$. The ring $C$ is reduced by Step 2, so $D$ is reduced: if $(c/a)^n=0$, some nonzero $b\in A$ kills $c^n$; then $(bc)^n=0$, whence $bc=0$ and $c/a=0$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/K$. The base change $Y_{\bar\eta}\to(Q_G)_{\bar\eta}$ is surjective. All points of its source lie in one $G$-orbit, and invariance makes their images equal; therefore its target is a singleton. Also $(Q_G)_{\bar\eta}\to(Q_G)_\eta$ is surjective, being the base change of the surjection $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}D$ is a nonempty singleton, in particular irreducible. The irreducible-spectrum criterion makes the nilradical of $D$ prime. Reducedness makes it zero, so $D$ is a domain. A finite-dimensional domain over a field is a field; denote it by $L$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, p.151, reduced generic quotient; Stacks 01WL, 01S1, 00ES; localization computation written out

proof.text: We show $L/K$ is purely inseparable. The finite algebra $D\otimes_K\Omega$ has singleton spectrum by Step 4. Its residue field is a finite-dimensional extension of $\Omega$: the quotient by its prime is a finite-dimensional domain, hence already a field. Such an extension of an algebraically closed field is trivial. Consequently there is exactly one $\Omega$-point of this singleton scheme, equivalently exactly one $K$-algebra map $t:L\to\Omega$. Existence can also be read directly from the integral geometric-point existence lemma applied to the zero prime of $L$, since the finite map $K\to L$ is integral. Apply the unique-geometric-point pure-residue lemma to $K\to L$, this $t$, and $K\to\Omega$. Every competing extension with the same kernel equals $t$, as just proved; both kernels are zero. The residue fields are therefore $K$ and $L$, and its conclusion is precisely that $L/K$ is purely inseparable. This proves the asserted generic-fibre clause for every $B_i$.

source.place: Tag 09GR, lemma-algebraically-closed; geometric-point refinement in WeilConjectures/Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/GeometricPoint.lean (the two cited DAG statements), the finite extension argument also follows 09HJ and 030K

proof.text: To apply the power-localization lemma we must check that $C$ itself is a domain, not merely its generic algebra. Write $h^{-1}U_i=\operatorname{Spec}S$, finite over $A$. This is an invariant open, so its quotient is $\operatorname{Spec}(S^G)$ and $C=S^G\subseteq S$. The ring $S$ is reduced. Each minimal prime of $S$ is the generic point of a component of this open of $Y$ and hence maps to the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Thus every nonzero $a\in A$ lies in no minimal prime of $S$. By the reduced-zerodivisor criterion multiplication by $a$ on $S$ is injective. It is then injective on $C\subseteq S$ as well. The fraction criterion for localization gives an injection $C\hookrightarrow C\otimes_AK=L$. Surjectivity of $h$ ensures $S\ne0$, so the same argument makes $A\hookrightarrow C$ injective. Hence $C$ is a domain, and $\operatorname{Frac}C=L$: the localization $C\otimes_AK$ is already a field, every fraction $c/a$ belongs to $\operatorname{Frac}C$, and every inverse of a nonzero element of $C$ belongs to this field. No commutation of invariants with nonflat base change was used.

source.place: Tag 00EW, lemma-reduced-ring-sub-product-fields (3); ILO IX 1.4, invariant affine quotient charts; explicit generic-localization injection

proof.text: Now $A$ is a Noetherian domain, $C$ is a finite $A$-algebra which is a domain, and their fraction fields are $K\subseteq L$ with $L/K$ finite purely inseparable. Apply the power-in-base localization lemma to obtain $s_i\in A\setminus\{0\}$. In characteristic zero it identifies $C[1/s_i]$ with $A[1/s_i]$. In characteristic $p>0$, each $c\in C[1/s_i]$ has $c^{p^n}$ in the base ring for some $n$. If two homomorphisms from $C[1/s_i]$ to any field agree on $A[1/s_i]$, their values on $c$ have equal $p^n$-th powers, hence are equal: in a field $(u-v)^{p^n}=0$ implies $u=v$. Thus maps from the spectrum of any field into the source over the base are unique. The field-valued-point criterion for radicial morphisms therefore makes $\operatorname{Spec}C[1/s_i]\to\operatorname{Spec}A[1/s_i]$ universally injective; in characteristic zero it is already an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BR5, purely inseparable power calculation; morphisms.tex Tag 01S4, lemma-universally-injective, field-valued-point criterion

proof.text: Set $U=\coprod_iD(s_i)\subseteq B$. Each $s_i$ is nonzero in the component domain, so $D(s_i)$ is nonempty and contains its generic point; their union is dense and contains every generic point of $B$. Restriction preserves finiteness of both $h$ and $d_G$, by finite base change. Surjectivity of $d_G$ from Step 2 persists under restriction by the surjective-base-change lemma, applied to the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow B$. A finite morphism is integral by the finite-algebra integrality theorem on each affine chart. Step 7 makes $d_G$ universally injective on these disjoint target components, hence globally (after any base change, points with the same image lie over the same component). The integral-radicial-surjective criterion now says that $Q_G\times_BU\to U$ is a universal homeomorphism. All quotient properties were supplied before shrinking and hold for every subgroup, while the generic field calculation of Steps 4--5 applies to every integral component.
